column1: # Reviewed USDA FoodData Central picks.
# One line per canonical ingredient: name <TAB> fdcId <TAB> description.
# `mix usda.migration --picks priv/repo/usda/picks.tsv` turns this into a
# migration, and refuses to run if an id no longer returns the description
# recorded here.
# This file is the decision log. `mix usda.candidates` proposes; a person
# picks. That split exists because FoodData Central's search ranks by text
# similarity, not identity -- left to its own devices it chose "Chewing gum"
# for xanthan gum, "Oil, walnut" for walnut, and "Cabbage, kimchi" over
# "Cabbage, raw". Every id below was read against the ingredient and the unit
# the stored recipes actually use.
# Ingredients deliberately NOT here are listed at the bottom, with why.
# --- Accepted by the picker and checked by hand -----------------------------
cheddar
gruyere
cardamom
whole milk ricotta
ground cloves
horseradish
radicchio
tomatillo
poppy seeds
# --- Held by the picker, resolved by hand -----------------------------------
# Brown sugar is brown sugar; FDC does not split light from dark, and the two
# differ negligibly in nutrition. Carries cup packed = 220 g, which is the unit
# 4,362 of these rows use.
light brown sugar
# "Yogurt, plain, whole milk". The higher-ranked 2259793 has no calorie value.
whole milk yogurt
# Search put peppercorn salad dressing and a Hormel pork tenderloin first.
# This is the spice, with tbsp and tsp ground weights -- the units 984 of these
# rows use.
black peppercorns
peppercorns
# "Cabbage, kimchi" ranked above this. The raw record is the one carrying
# head, medium = 908 g, which is what 900 rows ask for.
cabbage
# head, medium = 839 g. The higher-ranked 2346408 has the same description and
# no calorie value, which is why the id is pinned alongside the description.
red cabbage
# Fresh herbs, not the dried spice. The stored lines count these by the sprig,
# the bunch and the leaf, which is the fresh form; the dried spice records run
# 6-12x the calories per gram.
cilantro
basil
parsley
thyme
# Raw, not frozen or cooked.
asparagus
# "Fennel, bulb, raw" -- bulb = 234 g, and 1,785 rows say "1 fennel bulb".
# The higher-ranked 2747655 has the same description but no calorie value.
fennel
# FDC has no Persian cucumber. Nutrition per 100 g is the same cucumber; the
# per-cucumber weight is not taken, because a Persian cucumber is roughly a
# third the size of the 8-1/4" one this record measures.
persian cucumber
# The zest, not the juice -- search offered bottled lemon juice first.
lemon zest
# fresno chile (1,705 rows)   FDC's best offer was sriracha. No fresh Fresno
#                             record; a sibling copy from another fresh chile
#                             is the better answer.
# panko breadcrumbs (1,261)   No FoodData Central record at all.
# xanthan gum (734)           No record. "Chewing gum" is not a substitute.
# new mexico chile powder     No record; search returned baobab powder.
# cinnamon (996)              Needs the weight of one cinnamon stick. FDC has
#                             ground cinnamon only, and search returned
#                             cinnamon bread and bagels.
# sage (655)                  Needs fresh sage by the bunch; FDC surfaced only
#                             the dried ground spice.
# parmesan (1,030)            The 1,026 rows are "1 Parmesan rind", which is
#                             simmered and removed rather than eaten. Probably
#                             a role question, not a density one.
# pullman bread (797)         Needs a plain white sandwich loaf slice; search
#                             returned cheese, cinnamon and egg breads.
# ham (803)                   Needs a sliced ham weight; the top record is
#                             minced ham, a different product.
# coconut flakes (670)        FDC has sweetened desiccated coconut; recipes
#                             usually mean unsweetened. Genuinely ambiguous.
